We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation (attach sulfonyl chloride to aniline). (2) amide formation via coupling of carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) with aniline. (3) Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (N-phenyl). Gives precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C= C-COOH attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the same aniline? Actually sulfonamide attaches to the other phenyl ring (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the one with methyl). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the same aniline? Wait structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (first phenyl). The sulfonyl group attaches to second phenyl which also has the unsaturated amide side chain. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is the same as the aniline that is attached to the sulfonyl? Actually the nitrogen is part of the sulfonamide linking the two phenyls: p-tolyl-N-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline. So the nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl and to sulfonyl S. So the sulfonamide formation is between p-tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl (c2ccc...). So we need sulfonyl chloride of that phenyl (with the unsaturated amide side chain). So step: sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) reacts with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect sulfonamide bond between N and S, giving p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) where aryl contains the unsaturated amide side chain.

Then disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (the aniline is c3ccccc3N). That gives α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to aryl (the same aryl as sulfonyl chloride) and aniline.

Then disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid via Doebner modification (reverse). So aldehyde is the aryl aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid.

Thus we have three steps.
